# Exit Eval: Vendor / INVITE, ACCOUNT & ACCESS BOUNDARIES

> Wave 6 | 7 scenarios | Evaluated: 2026-05-25
> Mode: Solo (NEEDS-DEVELOPER-REVIEW)

---

## Scenario #1: Receive the vendor invite

**Original classification:** Bridgeable
**Reclassified to:** Bridgeable

**Why vendor leaves:** The vendor must open their email client to receive and click the invite URL. ChefFlow generates the token and URL (`generateVendorInvite` in `lib/vendors/invite-actions.ts`), but delivery happens outside the app. The vendor's first touchpoint with ChefFlow IS the email, so the email IS the onboarding surface.

**Context ChefFlow has:**

- Vendor name, email, type, phone, address (`vendors` table)
- Chef relationship (tenant_id via `vendors.chefId`)
- Invite token, expiry (7 days), creation timestamp (`vendor_invitations` table)
- Legal policies (privacy + vendor agreement links embedded in signup)

**Data source?** No. Email delivery is an outbound action, not a data lookup. The invite email is generated by the chef-side action.

**Client-collaborative angle:** Not applicable. The chef initiates the invite. The vendor just needs to find and click it. No Circle involvement.

**Physical reality:** Standard screen/email workflow. Vendor is at a desk or checking phone. No kitchen/hands-free needs at this moment.

**Compounding:** Low. One-time action per vendor-chef relationship. Once claimed, never repeated.

**Solution design:**

- Ensure invite emails are branded, mobile-friendly, and contain the chef's name/business for recognition
- Add invite delivery status tracking (sent, opened, clicked, expired) visible to the chef
- Make the invite URL resumable: if the vendor clicks but doesn't finish signup, the URL still works until expiry
- Add a "having trouble?" link in the invite email that shows the masked invited email and a contact path

**Where it appears:**

- Vendor's email inbox (the invite itself)
- `/auth/vendor-signup?token=...` (the landing page)
- Chef-side vendor management (invite status)

**What remains as permanent exit:**
The vendor will always leave to open their email client to find the invite. Email IS the delivery channel. ChefFlow's job is to make the email unmissable and the link reliable.

**Priority:** Medium frequency (once per vendor onboarding) x Low effort = Low-priority improvement
**Spec needed?** No

## Scenario #2: Find a lost invite

**Original classification:** Reducible
**Reclassified to:** Reducible

**Why vendor leaves:** The vendor lost or cannot find the original invite email. They resort to searching email, calling the chef, or texting. Currently there is no self-service "resend invite" or "check my invite status" flow. The only path is the chef generating a new invite via `generateVendorInvite`.

**Context ChefFlow has:**

- The original invite record: email, token hash, expiry, used_at status (`vendor_invitations` table)
- The vendor's email address (`vendors.email`)
- Whether the invite was already claimed (`used_at` field)
- Whether the invite expired (`expires_at` field)

**Data source?** No external data needed. ChefFlow owns all invite state.

**Client-collaborative angle:** The chef can resend. But the vendor should be able to self-service without bothering the chef. A "Request new invite" page where the vendor enters their email and the system checks for a valid pending invite, then resends or regenerates, would eliminate this exit.

**Physical reality:** Screen-based. Vendor is at a computer or phone. Standard web flow.

**Compounding:** Low. One-time per vendor. But multiplied across many vendors, it creates support friction for the chef.

**Solution design:**

- Add `/auth/vendor-invite-status` page where vendor enters email to check invite state
- If invite exists and is not expired: resend the email automatically
- If invite expired: show "expired, contact your chef" with the chef's business name and a button to request a new one
- Chef-side: add "Resend Invite" button on vendor detail page (currently only `generateVendorInvite` exists, no resend helper)
- Show invite status on chef's vendor list (pending, expired, claimed)

**Where it appears:**

- `/auth/vendor-signup` expired token error page (currently shows generic "invalid or expired" with only a sign-in link)
- Chef-side vendor management page
- New `/auth/vendor-invite-status` lookup page

**What remains as permanent exit:**
Vendor still opens email to actually click the link. But the "hunting" exit (searching email, calling chef) is eliminated.

**Priority:** Medium frequency (happens to ~20% of invitees) x Low effort = Medium rank signal
**Spec needed?** No (straightforward resend flow, no architectural decisions)

## Scenario #3: Confirm which email was invited

**Original classification:** Bridgeable
**Reclassified to:** Reducible

**Why vendor leaves:** `claimVendorInvite` requires the submitted email to match the invited email (case-insensitive comparison at line 87 of `lib/vendors/invite-actions.ts`). If the vendor uses a different email (personal vs business, typo, etc.), they get "Email does not match the invitation" error. They then call or email the chef to ask "which email did you invite?" Currently the error message gives no hint about which email was expected.

**Context ChefFlow has:**

- The exact invited email address (stored in `vendor_invitations.email`)
- The vendor's email from the `vendors` table (which should match)
- The invite token (proves the vendor has legitimate access to the link)

**Data source?** No. ChefFlow owns this data entirely.

**Client-collaborative angle:** Not applicable. This is purely between ChefFlow and the vendor. The system knows the answer.

**Physical reality:** Screen-based. Vendor is filling out a form.

**Compounding:** Low. One-time onboarding issue. But very frustrating when it happens.

**Solution design:**

- On email mismatch error, show a masked version of the invited email (e.g., "d\*\*\*@gmail.com") so the vendor recognizes which account was invited
- Add a "Not your email? Contact [Chef Business Name]" link below the error
- Pre-fill the email field from the invite record when the token is valid (the vendor just needs to confirm, not guess)
- If the vendor entity has a `contactName`, show it in the signup form as context ("Invited as: [business name]")

**Where it appears:**

- `/auth/vendor-signup` form (email field and error state)
- Error message after email mismatch

**What remains as permanent exit:**
If the vendor truly needs a different email invited (e.g., they changed business email), they still contact the chef. But the "which email was it?" confusion exit is eliminated.

**Priority:** Low frequency (happens to ~5-10% of invitees) x Very low effort = Medium rank signal
**Spec needed?** No

## Scenario #4: Store or retrieve password

**Original classification:** Permanent
**Reclassified to:** Permanent

**Why vendor leaves:** Credential storage is inherently external to ChefFlow. Vendors use browser keychains, password managers (1Password, LastPass, etc.), or their own memory. ChefFlow creates the password via bcrypt hash (`hash(password, 12)` in `claimVendorInvite`) but correctly never stores or displays plaintext. The vendor must manage their own credential lifecycle.

**Context ChefFlow has:**

- The hashed password (bcrypt, irreversible)
- The email associated with the account
- Password reset flow exists (`/auth/forgot-password` page, `requestPasswordReset` action in `lib/auth/actions.ts`)

**Data source?** No. This is a user behavior/tooling choice, not a data problem.

**Client-collaborative angle:** None. Password management is personal.

**Physical reality:** Standard credential management workflow. No kitchen/hands-free relevance.

**Compounding:** None. One password per account.

**Solution design:**

- Ensure signup form has proper `autocomplete="new-password"` attribute so browsers/password managers offer to save (partially done)
- Ensure sign-in form has proper `autocomplete="current-password"` for retrieval
- Consider passkey/WebAuthn support in the future to eliminate passwords entirely
- Ensure the forgot-password flow works for vendor accounts (currently generic, should work)

**Where it appears:**

- `/auth/vendor-signup` (password creation moment)
- `/auth/signin?portal=vendor` (password retrieval moment)
- Browser/OS password manager prompts

**What remains as permanent exit:**
The vendor will always use an external credential store. This is correct behavior. ChefFlow's job is to be a well-behaved web app that plays nicely with password managers and offers account recovery.

**Priority:** High frequency (every login) x Zero effort (already works) = No action needed
**Spec needed?** No

## Scenario #5: Resolve sign-in trouble

**Original classification:** Reducible
**Reclassified to:** Reducible

**Why vendor leaves:** When a vendor cannot sign in, there is no vendor-specific help surface. The generic `/auth/forgot-password` page exists and should work for vendor accounts (same `auth.users` table), but the vendor portal has no visible "having trouble?" link, no account recovery guidance, and no support intake. The vendor calls or emails the chef. The chef has no tools to diagnose vendor account issues.

**Context ChefFlow has:**

- Whether the vendor account exists (`auth.users` table)
- Whether the vendor role is active (`user_roles` table, `vendors.status`)
- Whether the invite was claimed (`vendor_invitations.used_at`)
- Password reset infrastructure (`/auth/forgot-password`, `requestPasswordReset`)
- The invited email (for mismatch diagnosis)

**Data source?** No. All account state is internal to ChefFlow.

**Client-collaborative angle:** The chef could be notified when a vendor is having access trouble, but this is a system problem, not a collaboration opportunity.

**Physical reality:** Screen-based. Vendor is at a computer or phone trying to log in.

**Compounding:** Medium. A vendor who has trouble once will have trouble again if the root cause (wrong email, inactive account, expired session) is not surfaced clearly.

**Solution design:**

- Add "Having trouble signing in?" link on `/auth/signin?portal=vendor` that leads to a vendor-specific help page
- The help page should diagnose: (a) forgot password -> reset flow, (b) don't have an account -> explain invite process, (c) account inactive -> suggest contacting chef
- Chef-side: add vendor account status visibility (active, inactive, last login, invite status)
- Chef-side: add "Reset vendor password" or "Deactivate/reactivate vendor account" actions
- Add clear error messages for inactive vendor accounts (currently redirects to signin silently when `vendor.status !== 'active'`)

**Where it appears:**

- `/auth/signin` page (vendor portal variant)
- `/auth/forgot-password` (already exists, works for all roles)
- Chef-side vendor management (account status tools)
- New vendor help/troubleshooting page

**What remains as permanent exit:**
If the vendor's email provider is down or they lost access to the email entirely, they must contact the chef through external channels. This is an edge case.

**Priority:** Medium frequency (10-15% of vendors hit access issues) x Low effort = Medium-high rank signal
**Spec needed?** No (incremental UX improvements, not a new system)

## Scenario #6: Change business user access

**Original classification:** Reducible
**Reclassified to:** Partially Reducible

**Why vendor leaves:** A vendor business may have multiple people who need portal access (owner, sales rep, delivery coordinator). Currently the vendor role maps 1:1 to a single `vendors` entity via `user_roles`. There is no vendor-side user/contact management. If a new person at the vendor company needs access, or an old one needs removal, the vendor contacts the chef by email/phone. The chef has no UI for managing multiple users per vendor either.

**Context ChefFlow has:**

- The vendor entity (one record per supplier in `vendors` table)
- The user-role binding (`user_roles` with role='vendor', entity_id=vendor.id)
- Multi-role infrastructure already exists (migration `20260515000001` removed single-role constraint)
- The `vendors` table has `contactName` field (singular) but no multi-contact support

**Data source?** No. This is an internal access control problem.

**Client-collaborative angle:** None. This is vendor-internal team management.

**Physical reality:** Administrative task. Desktop/screen-based.

**Compounding:** High. Vendor team changes are ongoing (new hires, role changes, departures). A self-service system pays dividends over the lifetime of the relationship.

**Solution design:**

- Phase 1 (chef-controlled): Chef can invite additional users to the same vendor entity (create multiple `user_roles` entries pointing to same `vendors.id`)
- Phase 2 (vendor-managed): Vendor admin can invite team members and revoke access from within the portal
- Add a vendor contacts/team section in `/vendor/profile`
- Add activity log per vendor user (who did what)
- Consider a "vendor admin" sub-role that can manage other vendor users vs. a "vendor user" who can only view/act on orders

**Where it appears:**

- `/vendor/profile` (team section, future)
- Chef-side vendor detail page (invite additional users)
- Vendor portal header (shows who is logged in)

**What remains as permanent exit:**
For now, the chef must authorize all vendor user additions. The vendor contacts the chef to request access changes. Full vendor self-service team management is a Phase 2 feature.

**Priority:** Low frequency (vendor team changes are rare per vendor) x Medium effort = Low-medium rank signal
**Spec needed?** Yes (multi-user vendor accounts touch auth, RLS, and UI across both sides). However, this is a later-phase feature; no spec written now.

## Scenario #7: Switch between multiple chef accounts

**Original classification:** Reducible
**Reclassified to:** Reducible

**Why vendor leaves:** A supplier (e.g., a produce distributor) may serve multiple ChefFlow chefs. Currently the vendor context is tenant-scoped: `requireVendor()` resolves to ONE `vendorId` via `user_roles`. The `RoleSwitcher` component (`components/shared/role-switcher.tsx`) already exists in the vendor layout and supports switching between roles. The multi-role migration (`20260515000001`) allows multiple `user_roles` entries per `auth_user_id`. So if the same email is invited by multiple chefs, they would have multiple vendor role entries and COULD switch between them.

**Context ChefFlow has:**

- Multi-role infrastructure: `user_roles` allows multiple vendor roles per user (unique constraint is on `auth_user_id + role + entity_id`, not on `auth_user_id + role`)
- `RoleSwitcher` component renders in vendor layout, shows when `availableRoleCount > 1`
- `switchRole` action sets `chefflow-active-role-id` cookie to select which role is active
- `getAvailableRoles` returns all roles for the current user
- `getHomePathForRole('vendor')` returns the vendor dashboard path

**Data source?** No. Fully internal.

**Client-collaborative angle:** None. This is vendor-side UX.

**Physical reality:** Standard screen interaction. Quick context switch.

**Compounding:** High for suppliers serving many chefs. Each additional chef relationship compounds the value of a seamless switcher.

**Solution design:**

- The core infrastructure already exists (`RoleSwitcher` + multi-role + `switchRole` action)
- However, `requireVendor()` in `lib/auth/get-user.ts` currently does `.limit(1)` on `user_roles` query, which may not respect the active role cookie for the vendor case
- Verify that `requireVendor` reads the `chefflow-active-role-id` cookie to pick the correct vendor role when multiple exist
- Add chef business name to the role switcher label (currently shows generic "Vendor" for all vendor roles)
- The switcher dropdown should show "Vendor (Chef Name 1)" and "Vendor (Chef Name 2)" to distinguish contexts
- Test: invite same email from two different chef accounts, verify switching works

**Where it appears:**

- Vendor layout header (`RoleSwitcher` component)
- `/vendor/dashboard` (shows data scoped to active vendor context)
- All vendor pages (scoped by `vendorId` from active role)

**What remains as permanent exit:**
If the vendor has relationships with chefs NOT on ChefFlow, they still manage those externally. But for all ChefFlow chefs, switching is in-app.

**Priority:** Low frequency (few vendors serve multiple ChefFlow chefs today) x Low effort (infra exists, needs polish) = Low rank signal now, scales later
**Spec needed?** No (infrastructure exists; needs testing and label improvements)
